nodes.name: Schedule
nodes.notes:
What: Starts the publisher on a timer so due posts go out without anyone opening n8n.
In: No input; the rule is an interval, field hours with hoursInterval 1, so once an hour in Africa/Cairo.
Out: A single trigger item with no request body, which starts the run.
Why: The workflow timezone is Africa/Cairo in settings, and the rule sets no explicit minute of the hour.

nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes:
What: Lets a person or another workflow start a publish run on demand over HTTP.
In: A POST to the path instabay-publish, with an optional JSON body carrying a force flag.
Out: One item holding the request, including its body, passed to Init Run.
Why: responseMode is lastNode, so the caller waits and receives the final node output as the reply.

nodes.name: Init Run
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that stamps the run with an id and a start time and reads the force flag from the body.
In: The single trigger item; only the webhook path supplies a body, the schedule item has none.
Out: One item with run_id of wf3- plus the execution id, started_at as an ISO time, and force as a boolean.
Why: force accepts boolean true and the string true, because a webhook body often sends the flag as text.

nodes.name: Read Config
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the Config tab of the project spreadsheet with the read operation.
In: The single item from Init Run; document id 1idaFANX0dJtbl-ww6-Bca6WAFU6BUmwTon_wdxizXwk.
Out: One item per Config row, each carrying a key column and a value column.
Why: executeOnce is on and maxTries is 2, so settings are fetched once per run with one retry on failure.

nodes.name: Read Calendar
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the Calendar tab, which holds every planned post and its status.
In: The Config rows from Read Config; executeOnce means it runs once, on the first item only.
Out: One item per Calendar row, with fields such as post_id, status, publish_at, format and image_url.
Why: Same spreadsheet and the same executeOnce plus maxTries 2, so one run makes one read here.

nodes.name: Select Due
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that keeps approved Calendar rows whose publish_at has passed, and attaches API settings.
In: Rows from Read Calendar, the key and value rows from Read Config, and the force flag from Init Run.
Out: One item per due post: the row plus publish_mode, ig_user_id, graph_api_version and ig_access_token.
Why: force true skips the publish_at test, and publish_mode falls back to dry_run when Config has no value.

nodes.name: Publish Mode?
nodes.notes:
What: Splits the run into a dry run branch and a live publishing branch on one Config value.
In: Each due post item from Select Due, carrying its publish_mode value.
Out: DryRun output when publish_mode equals dry_run, Live output when it equals live; item unchanged.
Why: No fallback output is set, so a typo or an empty setting drops the post instead of publishing it.

nodes.name: Simulate Publish
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that builds the exact Graph API call sequence a real publish would make, without sending it.
In: One due post at a time from the DryRun output, with format, image_url, captions, hashtags and topic.
Out: post_id, status published, media_id of DRYRUN_ plus the post id, published_at and api_payload_log.
Why: The log opens with a step 0 quota check; a format that is not reel or carousel logs the image calls.

nodes.name: Check Quota
nodes.notes:
What: GET on the Graph API content_publishing_limit edge for the IG user, reading quota_usage.
In: One item from the Live output of Publish Mode?, supplying version, user id and token to the URL.
Out: The raw Graph reply, which Quota Guard reads as data[0].quota_usage.
Why: The access token travels in the URL query string from Config, not through an n8n credential.

nodes.name: Quota Guard
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that throws at the posting limit, then puts the original post row back on the item.
In: The Graph quota reply for one item, plus the matching item pulled back from Publish Mode? by name.
Out: The original due post item, unchanged, when quota_usage is missing or below 100.
Why: It throws only at 100 or more, so a reply it cannot read is not treated as hitting the limit.

nodes.name: Media Type?
nodes.notes:
What: Routes each post to the reel, image or carousel publishing path on the format field.
In: One due post item from Quota Guard, carrying its format value.
Out: Reel output for reel, Image for image, Carousel for carousel; the item passes through unchanged.
Why: No fallback output is set, so an unknown format is dropped instead of taking the wrong path.

nodes.name: Create Reel Container
nodes.notes:
What: POSTs to the Graph API media edge to create an unpublished REELS container with share_to_feed true.
In: One reel item from Media Type?; the body sends video_url, captions, hashtags, share_to_feed and token.
Out: The Graph reply holding the new container id.
Why: A missing video_url sends the literal SET_PUBLIC_HTTPS_VIDEO_URL, so the call fails loudly, not quietly.

nodes.name: Wait 60s
nodes.notes:
What: Pauses the reel branch for one minute so Instagram can process the uploaded video.
In: The container reply from Create Reel Container, and every retry sent back by Poll Guard.
Out: The same item, released after a 60 second time interval, into Poll Container.
Why: The dry run log notes that publishing while IN_PROGRESS returns error 9007, so the run waits first.

nodes.name: Poll Container
nodes.notes:
What: GETs the container object with fields set to status_code, to see whether the reel is ready.
In: Values read by node name: container id from Create Reel Container, version and token from Select Due.
Out: The Graph reply carrying status_code, which the next node compares against FINISHED.
Why: The container reply holds only an id, so the version and token are read back from Select Due.

nodes.name: Container Ready?
nodes.notes:
What: Checks whether the reel container reports FINISHED and sends it forward or back to wait.
In: The poll reply for one reel, with its status_code string.
Out: True branch goes to Publish Reel; false branch goes to Poll Guard and back into the wait loop.
Why: The test is a strict string equals on FINISHED, so any other status loops round again.

nodes.name: Poll Guard
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that counts loop passes and throws once the reel has been polled too many times.
In: The not ready items from the false output of Container Ready?, plus the node run index.
Out: The same items unchanged, sent back to Wait 60s, unless the run index has already reached 10.
Why: It throws instead of marking the row, so a stuck reel ends the run with no Calendar update.

parameters.jsCode:
if ($runIndex >= 10) throw new Error('Reel container not ready after 10 polls (~10 min) - marking failed');
return $input.all();

nodes.name: Publish Reel
nodes.notes:
What: POSTs to the Graph API media_publish edge of the IG user to publish the finished reel container.
In: creation_id read from Create Reel Container, with version, user id and token read from Select Due.
Out: The Graph reply carrying the new media id.
Why: It runs only on the FINISHED branch, so the container is published after encoding has completed.

nodes.name: Create Image Container
nodes.notes:
What: POSTs to the Graph API media edge of the IG user to create an unpublished single image container.
In: One item from the Image output of Media Type?, with image_url, the two captions, hashtags and topic.
Out: The Graph reply holding the new container id.
Why: The caption joins caption_en, caption_ar and hashtags, and alt_text is filled from the topic field.

nodes.name: Publish Image
nodes.notes:
What: POSTs to the Graph API media_publish edge to publish the image container straight away.
In: creation_id from the container reply on the current item; version, user id and token from Select Due.
Out: The Graph reply carrying the new media id.
Why: The image path has no polling, so it is two calls where the reel path adds a wait and poll loop.

nodes.name: Carousel TODO
nodes.notes:
What: Set node that marks a carousel post as failed and records why the live path was not built.
In: One item from the Carousel output of Media Type?.
Out: Only four fields: post_id, status failed, an empty media_id, and a note in api_payload_log.
Why: The note names the missing child container loop, so the gap sits in the data instead of being hidden.

assignments.name: api_payload_log
assignments.value: live carousel path not implemented in this time-box (needs child-container loop); publish carousels via dry_run or extend the workflow

nodes.name: Normalize Live Result
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that turns any of the three live branch replies into one common result shape.
In: One reply at a time from Publish Reel, Publish Image or Carousel TODO, plus the row from Media Type?.
Out: post_id, status published or failed, media_id, published_at and api_payload_log.
Why: This shape matches what Simulate Publish emits, so the sheet writer never needs to know which path ran.

nodes.name: Update Published
nodes.notes:
What: Writes each result back onto the Calendar row of the post it belongs to.
In: Result items from Simulate Publish or Normalize Live Result, both carrying the same five fields.
Out: Updated rows on the Calendar tab, using appendOrUpdate matched on the post_id column.
Why: Matching on post_id means a rerun overwrites the same row instead of adding duplicates.

nodes.name: Run Stats
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that builds one summary row for the run, with timing, post count and the mode used.
In: Every item from Update Published, run_id and started_at from Init Run, publish_mode from Select Due.
Out: One row with run_id, workflow WF3-publisher, batch_id, timings, duration_s, posts_count and notes.
Why: batch_id comes from a regex on the first post_id, and the two cost fields are written empty.

nodes.name: Log Run
nodes.notes:
What: Appends the run summary as a new line in the run history tab.
In: The single summary item from Run Stats.
Out: One new row on the RunLog tab of the same spreadsheet, appended with auto mapped input data.
Why: Append rather than update, so every run keeps its own line; maxTries 2 gives one retry if Sheets fails.
